newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index dips 0.3 points on VSZ loss.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index dips 0.3 points on VSZ loss.

text.p: Slovakia's Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) closed the week lower in moderate trading on Friday, with the 16-share SAX index pulled down by steel maker VSZ.
The index closed at 169.25 points, down 0.3 from Thursday's close.
VSZ, usually the most liquid first-tier issue, eased four crowns to 646, on volume of just 42 shares.
A new division of markets on the BSE, which became effective on Friday, so far appeared to have no immediate effect on trading.

Direct trades continued overshadowing the sessions on the bourse's listed, registered and free markets, as turnover of more than 780 million crowns was recorded in direct deals, against some 300,000 crowns on the automated floors.
However, brokers have said the BSE's new shape should contribute to transparency of the market.
A total of 15 shares traded in commercial bank VUB which closed unchanged at 1,270 crowns.
The most heavily-weighted issue in the SAX index, oil refinery Slovnaft, did not match any trades on Friday.
Overall, volume rose to 1.092 million shares, from 960,810 on Thursday, while turnover increased to 783.96 million crowns, from 448.46 million. -- Peter Javurek, Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402
